links.comparator_used: Label-only prompt without the structured NiTi file-group framework (model's built-in knowledge)
links.outcome: Clinical Appropriateness Score, strict concordance with expert-preferred file group, prohibited proprietary names, non-acceptable responses
links.effect: CAS rose from 75.0 to 80.6; strict concordance rose from 24.6% to 37.9%, with the gain concentrated among responses containing prohibited proprietary names (14.2% to 40.8%); non-acceptable responses fell from 7.1% to 3.3% (not statistically significant); no detectable concordance gain among terminology-compliant responses
links.tradeoff: Prohibited proprietary names in responses increased from 14.2% to 40.8% with the framework (terminology non-compliance)
links.quote: Structured prompting improved recommendation quality, but did not produce a detectable concordance gain among terminology-compliant responses.
